rituals.goal: Send one number through a two-rule orbit.
rituals.mission: Send one number through a two-rule orbit.
rituals.rule: Even → divide by 2; odd → multiply by 3 and add 1.
rituals.one_rule: Even → divide by 2; odd → multiply by 3 and add 1.

rituals.win: One starting number follows a deterministic alternating rule path all the way to 1.
rituals.mindBend: A tiny odd-even rule can generate a surprisingly long numerical journey. This demonstrates how complex-looking trajectories can arise from simple repeated operations.

rituals.safety: Keep the round within neutral examples for one pass. Stop at once if proof-seeking repetition develops; leave the puzzle unfinished.

rituals.goal: Solve one picture-puzzle row from its run clue.

rituals.rule: A clue of 3 means exactly three consecutive filled cells.

rituals.mindBend: A single nonogram row can be solved from the run constraint before individual cells are known. This traces how global structure can determine local answers.

rituals.safety: Limit this to neutral examples. If proof-seeking repetition shows up, do not continue; drop the puzzle before completion.

rituals.goal: Prove that one box must receive a repeat without knowing which box.

rituals.rule: Use only counts of items and categories.

rituals.goal: Grow a number chain that builds itself from its last two links.
rituals.mission: Grow a number chain that builds itself from its last two links.
rituals.rule: Each new number equals the previous two added together.
rituals.one_rule: Each new number equals the previous two added together.

rituals.goal: Fill the missing cells without repeating a symbol.
rituals.mission: Fill the missing cells without repeating a symbol.
rituals.rule: Each row and each column must contain A, B and C exactly once.
rituals.one_rule: Each row and each column must contain A, B and C exactly once.
rituals.play: Picture this 3×3 grid: Row 1 = A, B, blank. Row 2 = B, blank, A. Row 3 = blank, A, B. Fill the three blanks so every row and column contains A, B and C exactly once.
rituals.twist: Do not use guessing after a row or column forces the answer.
rituals.win: The three blanks resolve to C, C and C through row-and-column constraints.
rituals.mindBend: Latin-square constraints can determine a blank from intersecting row and column requirements. What changes is certainty created by structure rather than by guessing the cell.
rituals.mind_bend: Latin-square constraints can determine a blank from intersecting row and column requirements. What changes is certainty created by structure rather than by guessing the cell.
rituals.safety: Keep this to neutral examples. When perfection pressure appears, step out and switch to an ordinary activity.

rituals.goal: Make the invisible alternative cost appear beside the choice.
rituals.mission: Make the invisible alternative cost appear beside the choice.
rituals.rule: Use one scarce resource such as time or money.
rituals.one_rule: Use one scarce resource such as time or money.
rituals.play: Suppose you spend Saturday morning on Option A. Name the single best thing you would otherwise do with those same hours and place it beside A as the opportunity cost.
rituals.twist: Do not list every alternative—only the best forgone one.
rituals.win: The best forgone alternative becomes an explicit cost even when no money is spent.
rituals.mindBend: Choosing one use of scarce time or money silently chooses against its best alternative. Opportunity cost is part of the decision even when it is invisible.
rituals.mind_bend: Choosing one use of scarce time or money silently chooses against its best alternative. Opportunity cost is part of the decision even when it is invisible.
rituals.safety: Stay with low-stakes decision pressure. If urgent facts needing action show up, end there; use real-world guidance.

rituals.goal: Catch a streak trying to rewrite probability.
rituals.mission: Catch a streak trying to rewrite probability.
rituals.rule: Every fair coin flip remains independent.
rituals.one_rule: Every fair coin flip remains independent.
rituals.play: Imagine five fair-coin results: H-H-H-H-H. Before the sixth flip, notice whether TAILS feels 'due.' Then state the actual probability of tails on flip six.
rituals.twist: Do not average across the six flips; judge only the next one.
rituals.win: A streak-induced expectation separates from the unchanged 50/50 next-flip probability.
rituals.mindBend: A streak of identical coin outcomes does not alter the next fair flip. One implication is the mind’s tendency to mistake recent sequence for a change in independent probability.
rituals.mind_bend: A streak of identical coin outcomes does not alter the next fair flip. One implication is the mind’s tendency to mistake recent sequence for a change in independent probability.
rituals.safety: Work only with a low-stakes mental game. If self-judgment from frustration becomes noticeable, pause the exercise and move on without forcing a solution.

rituals.win: A set is filtered by divisibility structure instead of by surface appearance.
rituals.mindBend: Primality depends on divisors, not on whether a number merely looks odd or even. That clarifies why structural definition outranks a superficial shortcut.

rituals.goal: Decide whether the conclusion is forced by the premises.
rituals.mission: Decide whether the conclusion is forced by the premises.
rituals.play: Premise 1: All robins are birds. Premise 2: All birds are animals. Conclusion: All robins are animals. Decide VALID or NOT VALID.

GOAL
Decide whether the conclusion is forced by the premises.

ONE RULE
Use only the statements given.

PLAY
Premise 1: All robins are birds. Premise 2: All birds are animals. Conclusion: All robins are animals. Decide VALID or NOT VALID.

TWIST
Then explain the link in one short chain: robin → bird → animal.

WIN
The conclusion is accepted because class membership carries through both premises.

MIND BEND
A conclusion can be valid because class membership chains through the given premises. Logical entailment is something stricter than whether the conclusion merely sounds plausible.

SAFETY
Use a low-stakes mental game. Switch to an ordinary activity when proof-seeking repetition shows up; do not continue the task.

rituals.win: Values become a late tiebreaker, not vague override.

rituals.safety: Use only a safely pausable decision. If urgent facts needing action show up, pause the exercise and act on the urgent information.

rituals.goal: Watch an irrelevant number pull an estimate.
rituals.mission: Watch an irrelevant number pull an estimate.
rituals.rule: Use the same question twice; only the anchor changes.
rituals.one_rule: Use the same question twice; only the anchor changes.
rituals.play: Estimate the height of a typical adult door after first hearing '1 metre'. Then reset and estimate again after hearing '4 metres'. Do not look up the answer.
rituals.twist: Compare the two estimates, not which one is correct.
rituals.win: An irrelevant starting number visibly shifts a later judgement.
rituals.mindBend: A low or high number shown first can pull later estimates of the same quantity. Anchoring is numerical context contaminating judgment before evidence changes.
rituals.mind_bend: A low or high number shown first can pull later estimates of the same quantity. Anchoring is numerical context contaminating judgment before evidence changes.
rituals.safety: Work only with a nonurgent choice for one pass. If urgent facts needing action develop: switch to the real-world facts. Leave the exercise there.

rituals.name: MENTAL MAZE
rituals.unique_game_move: trace a shortest route through a small imagined grid maze without moving through blocked cells
rituals.recognition_cue: Mind play • Mental reset. ROUTER TAGS: creative creativity ideas idea bored mind play thought experiment flexibility creative creativity ideas idea bored mind play thought experiment flexibility creative creativity ideas idea bored mind play thought experiment flexibility
rituals.immediate_need: restore flexible thinking

rituals.goal: Navigate a tiny maze entirely in mind.
rituals.mission: Navigate a tiny maze entirely in mind.
rituals.rule: No diagonal moves; blocked cells cannot be entered.
rituals.one_rule: No diagonal moves; blocked cells cannot be entered.
rituals.play: Picture a 3×3 grid labelled A1 to C3. START at A1, EXIT at C3, and block B1 and B2. Find the shortest legal route using only up, down, left or right moves.
rituals.twist: Once you choose the blocks, do not move them.
rituals.win: A1 → A2 → A3 → B3 → C3 reaches the exit in four legal moves.
rituals.mindBend: A shortest maze route appears by respecting blocked cells and move rules. This indicates how efficient planning emerges from constraints rather than from imagining every possible path.
rituals.mind_bend: A shortest maze route appears by respecting blocked cells and move rules. This indicates how efficient planning emerges from constraints rather than from imagining every possible path.
rituals.safety: Stay with neutral examples for one pass. Do not continue if proof-seeking repetition develops; end the task without a personal rating.

rituals.goal: Make yesterday's effort lose its vote.
rituals.mission: Make yesterday's effort lose its vote.
rituals.rule: Past time or money cannot be counted as a future benefit.
rituals.one_rule: Past time or money cannot be counted as a future benefit.
rituals.play: Imagine you spent two hours on a project that now looks unhelpful. Compare CONTINUE and STOP using only what each option costs and gives from this moment forward.
rituals.twist: Every reason beginning with 'but I've already...' is disqualified.
rituals.win: The next move can be judged from future value rather than sunk effort.
rituals.mindBend: Past time or money cannot improve the future value of continuing. Sunk cost is history that feels relevant even when it cannot change what happens next.
rituals.mind_bend: Past time or money cannot improve the future value of continuing. Sunk cost is history that feels relevant even when it cannot change what happens next.
rituals.safety: Use one genuinely small action for this pass. When pushing through illness or exhaustion becomes noticeable, end it there and take a smaller practical action.

rituals.goal: Remember a tiny path as positions, not words.
rituals.mission: Remember a tiny path as positions, not words.
rituals.play: Imagine nine squares arranged in three rows and three columns. Flash these positions in order: top-left, centre, bottom-right, top-right. Clear them, then replay the four locations in the same order.
rituals.twist: Do not number or name the positions while rehearsing them.
rituals.win: A four-step spatial sequence is reproduced from location memory alone.
rituals.mindBend: A sequence of locations can be retained without naming or numbering them. Spatial working memory is a system that can operate independently of verbal rehearsal.
rituals.mind_bend: A sequence of locations can be retained without naming or numbering them. Spatial working memory is a system that can operate independently of verbal rehearsal.
rituals.safety: Use low-stakes material. If repeated self-testing becomes noticeable, stop and use an external note.

rituals.goal: Move the finish line closer without changing the next step.
rituals.mission: Move the finish line closer without changing the next step.
rituals.rule: The next required action is unchanged across the two rounds.
rituals.one_rule: The next required action is unchanged across the two rounds.
rituals.play: Imagine a ten-step task where the next step is the same simple action. First picture yourself at step 1 of 10; then picture yourself at step 9 of 10. Compare the pull to perform that next action.
rituals.twist: Do not change reward, difficulty or time—only apparent progress.
rituals.win: Proximity to completion can change motivational pull while the next action remains identical.
rituals.mindBend: The same next action can feel easier when imagined near the finish than near the start. Apparent progress itself is an origin of motivational pull.
rituals.mind_bend: The same next action can feel easier when imagined near the finish than near the start. Apparent progress itself is an origin of motivational pull.
rituals.safety: Work only with a safe ordinary task. Rest or reassess the priority when the exercise shifts into pushing through illness or exhaustion; do not continue the task.
